title: Empty market groups are PRINTED, with counts — against the whole industry, deliberately
body: Empty market groups are PRINTED, with counts — against the whole industry, deliberately | **APPROVED — ALLEN, relayed 2026-08-17** · put at `calls-for-allen-2026-08-17.md` §2. **`CORNERS ….. 11` beside every group that has offers; `CORNERS ….. no prices offered` where the house is not pricing.** Every real book silently drops an empty group; **our law is that the slate must not be misrepresented, and `S86` measured NINE of fifteen market kinds with no reachable home.** Buys three things: the player can SEE the house is not offering corners today, **which is information the real books destroy**; the contents block becomes a fixed-length object rather than a shape-shifter; and **`C19`'s reachability stops being an invisible engineering promise and becomes a legible feature of the fiction.** *A racecard prints the race even when it is abandoned.* Costs about six lines, and BTTS has 5.8 rows of slack measured at `S87`. | `[M2] docs/design/calls-for-allen-2026-08-17.md` §2

title: The name-first hierarchy RATIFIED; the price's amber decided on a frame
body: The name-first hierarchy RATIFIED; the price's amber decided on a frame | **APPROVED — ALLEN, relayed 2026-08-17, taking this seat's split recommendation** · §4. **HALF ONE, RULED NOW: the market name leads in the typeset layer and the price sits right-aligned beside it. This is largely what the build already does — and it ARRIVED BY MIGRATION DRIFT, never as a decision** (`S86`/`S87`'s reads). **Ratifying costs nothing and buys the thing that matters: once a board is built price-first it is not cheaply reversed, and until now nothing stopped it drifting back.** It is also the diegetically correct hierarchy — *a form guide leads with the runner* — and it puts the **LINE** (printed, fixed, part of the form) against the **PRICE** (annotated, the house's mutable offer) along the exact seam the colour law already draws. **HALF TWO, DELIBERATELY NOT RULED FROM THE DESK: does the price take the amber?** The law says amber = money and a price is money, which argues yes; against it, **~80 amber prices on one sheet, and amber is also the ACTION colour — if everything is amber, nothing is.** **That is a read at distance and this seat has been wrong twice this week predicting instead of measuring. RULED: one sheet rendered BOTH WAYS, decided on the frame** — and the comparison frame **lands with the build** rather than being commissioned separately. **The seat's lean, on the record and not binding: yes.** `S92` strengthens it — at one offer per row the amber lands in a single column down the right edge, an annotation rail rather than scattered ink. | `[M2] docs/design/calls-for-allen-2026-08-17.md` §4

title: THE RAIL AT 700px — six destinations overflow; CORRECT SCORE folds into RESULT and the rail returns to FIVE
body: THE RAIL AT 700px — six destinations overflow; CORRECT SCORE folds into RESULT and the rail returns to FIVE | **RULED — DD 2026-08-17 batch 110**, on the surfaces build's measurement. **The spec's §9 said the ~9 capacity was *arithmetic on authored constants and has NEVER been measured* and told the build to measure it. It did: the usable width is 700px, not the ~996px the arithmetic assumed, and SIX destinations overflow. The flag worked; the number it guarded was wrong; and §3's "the headroom is deliberate" rested on it. §1.5.** **THE THREE OPTIONS OFFERED ARE ALL REFUSED, and two of them by rulings this seat already made.** **Shrinking type: REFUSED — the 13px product-fact floor is law and §8's no-shrinking-type stands.** **Tiering: REFUSED — the spec's own §5.2 says the rail stays ONE level, and the research is unambiguous that the double-tiered rail is DraftKings' most-criticised feature. A ruling made four hours ago is not a lever.** **Abbreviating `CORRECT SCORE`: REFUSED as unnecessary, which is the better reason — it treats the symptom.** **THE CAUSE IS THE SIXTH DESTINATION, NOT THE LONGEST NAME.** Six tabs carry 43 characters against today's working five at 28; **the excess is one whole tab plus thirteen characters, and removing the tab removes both.** **RULED: `CORRECT SCORE` FOLDS INTO `RESULT`. Five destinations — `RESULT · GOALS · CORNERS · CARDS · PLAYERS`.** **It is taxonomically BETTER, not a compromise: Correct Score IS a result market — the most specific one there is — and `RESULT` is a bet-type name holding abstractions, with `WinningMargin` already inside it as its near cousin.** **The arithmetic: the new five carry 30 characters against today's 28 — plus two characters across five tabs, against a rail whose five tabs already fit inside 700px with the last origin at 442. It fits by the same arithmetic that already works, rather than by a new allowance.** **AND NOTHING IS HIDDEN, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS CHEAP: §5.2's contents block names every market inside its group with its own line range, so `CORRECT SCORE` stays fully findable. The two-level contents was built precisely so the RAIL could flex without the vocabulary paying for it — this is the first time it has been asked to, and it is doing the job it was designed for.** **THE GATE STILL DECIDES: the build gates at real width and reports overflow rather than resolving it, which is exactly right and must not change. If five still overflows, abbreviation becomes live and comes back to this seat — but it is not reached for first.** | `[M2] docs/design/spec-market-surfaces-2026-08-17.md` §3

title: The rail ORDER — §5.2's order governs; §3's table is the stale half
body: The rail ORDER — §5.2's order governs; §3's table is the stale half | **RULED — DD 2026-08-18 batch 113**, resolving the spec's self-contradiction. **ORDER: `RESULT · GOALS · CORNERS · CARDS · CORRECT SCORE · PLAYERS`.** The lane built §3's table on the sound ground that a normative table outranks an illustration, **and it chose correctly on the evidence it had — but §3's table is the stale half and the illustration was the considered one.** **TWO REASONS, AND THEY POINT THE SAME WAY.** **(1) TAXONOMIC: §5.2's order runs the three COUNTABLE STATISTICS adjacently — `GOALS · CORNERS · CARDS` — and seats the abstract bet type after them. That is the SAME statistic-vs-bet-type seam §3 uses to justify the taxonomy in the first place**, so §3's table contradicts §3's own reasoning: it interleaves bet-type, statistic, bet-type, statistic, statistic and teaches the player nothing about the structure. **(2) POPULARITY, which is the RAIL's own ordering law** (the research transfer this seat ratified: *popularity leads the group rail; a stable printed order governs INSIDE a group*). **`CORRECT SCORE` is among the least-bet markets on the sheet and §3 seated it THIRD.** **CONFIRMED ON THE FRAME, not only argued:** on `S4`/`S5` the rail reads `RESULT · GOALS · CORRECT SCORE · CORNERS · CARDS · PLAYERS`, and the widest label on the rail sits wedged between two of the shortest, **breaking the `GOALS`/`CORNERS`/`CARDS` run visibly.** **The cost is the lane's own measurement — *low and mechanical, one array's order*, with every printed line range and folio number derived and nothing hand-edited.** The two contents frames re-shoot; that is the whole bill. **Taking the CHEAP correction while declining the expensive one (`S94-cl`) is deliberate and consistent, not inconsistent: the order is one array, the fold was a rebuild.** | `[M2] docs/design/spec-market-surfaces-2026-08-17.md` §3, §5.2

title: The strip's words are licensed by the RESOLVED SCENE, never the beat's type — and the remedy already existed
body: The strip's words are licensed by the RESOLVED SCENE, never the beat's type — and the remedy already existed | **RULED, and the fix is an EXISTING guard applied to a second family** — DD 2026-08-14 batch 68. Mechanism: `RenderEvent` stashes `_pendingFlavor`, `RevealBeatChrome` lands it into `_tFlavor` (**the strip — confirmed at `AtTier(ink, TierL2)`, T66's own tier**); the line comes from `SweatFlavor.Line` → `Base(e.Type, …)`, **selected by the beat's TYPE**, so a beat typed `Score` prints a goal sentence **whether or not the resolved scene contains a goal**. **`SweatFlavor.NeutralLine` ALREADY EXISTS for exactly this defect one market family over** — its own comment reads *"a count-market beat whose resolved scene carries no count event … corner/booking words would be a lie there"* (Sol, F_0.4.0 P3 r2) — **and the orchestrator already overrides with it for counts. The goal families never got the same override.** **THE LAW, stated generally because this is its second instance: a beat's WORDS are licensed by what the resolved scene actually contains, never by the beat's type label alone** — where the scene lacks the asserted event, the authored neutral line stands in. **Scope: every family that ASSERTS A GOAL** — `ScoreUp`, `ScoreDown`, and the finishing members of `BigUp`/`BigDown`; **the lead sweeps those four arrays string by string** and reports which assert a goal versus only a dangerous move (**this seat did not audit every line**). **The `NearMiss` overrides are already correct and are the model.** **Stale-carry vs fresh mis-selection is the lead's diagnosis to report — both are the same defect under the law and neither changes the remedy** | batch 68

title: `CashOut` overruns by 26.7px on `MARKET SUSPENDED` — a permanently marginal CONSTANT
body: `CashOut` overruns by 26.7px on `MARKET SUSPENDED` — a permanently marginal CONSTANT | **RULED — DEFECT; re-author the constant** · DD 2026-08-17 batch 104. **Box 241.0px, widest `MARKET SUSPENDED` 267.7px — OVER BY 26.7px.** §6.1's money control, one of its six ruled states, and `TV-12/13` gives that string the slot **exclusively**. **THIS IS A SOLVED CASE AND THE PRECEDENT IS OURS, VERBATIM:** `G1` on `BOTH TEAMS TO SCORE` — *a permanently marginal CONSTANT, no variable in it at all, so it was over budget on EVERY FRAME IT EVER DREW. One word clears it.* **A constant that overruns is not a risk, it is a defect on every frame**, and unlike a generated string it cannot be argued about — there is no pool, no widest case, no seed where it fits. **RULED: it is RE-AUTHORED. Not truncated (`T69`), and the box does not widen to fit a constant.** **`SUSPENDED` is the obvious candidate — the control IS the subject, so `MARKET` is the repeated half, and G1's own reasoning applies (`TO WIN`/`TO SCORE`: *the subject is not missing, it is simply not repeated*).** **NAMED AS A CANDIDATE AND NOT RULED AS THE STRING: it must be MEASURED before it is authored.** Dropping seven of sixteen characters will very probably clear 26.7px, and *very probably* is the word this studio has been wrong on twice this week. **The state must still be STATED, not carried by grey alone** — the standing law, and the market research records a production book independently arriving at it. **PROCESS, RECORDED BECAUSE IT IS WHY THE LANE IS WORTH HAVING: nobody asked the sweep for this.** It sits outside all three families and outside the sweep's scope, and the lane **measured it, refused to fix it, and routed it.** That is the behaviour, and a finding nobody commissioned is the most valuable kind an instrument produces. | `[TV] TvExtentSweep · §6.1 / TV-12/13`

title: `§6.7` ALREADY SPECIFIES THE BOUNDARY — and the leg boundary is the one place it does not fire
body: `§6.7` ALREADY SPECIFIES THE BOUNDARY — and the leg boundary is the one place it does not fire | **RULED — the defect's mechanism NAMED, and it is an existing clause not applied** · DD 2026-08-19 batch 128, measured on arm 2 at f066 → f068. **`§6.7` reads: *"Appears only once the stage and active-leg card have CLEARED. No score, clock, tape, event line, suspended label or prior offer survives into it."*** **EVERY ITEM ON THAT LIST SURVIVES THE LEG BOUNDARY: the score survives (`MALLARDS 0 — 0 MIDDLEMEN`); the clock survives AND REWINDS (`FT` → `1'`); the event line survives (`LEG 1 — WON` → *"Middlemen pin them deep — passes and patience."*); the suspended label survives and becomes a live offer (`SUSPENDED` → `CASH OUT $56`); the active-leg card never clears.** **The studio HAS a specified device for separating two tellings. It fires between TICKETS, and the one boundary that REPLAYS THE SAME FIXTURE gets a hard cut across two frames.** **AND THE ENDING SHARES A FRAME WITH THE NEXT LEG'S JEOPARDY: at f066 the surface reads `FT`, `LEG 1 — WON`, and — in the column beneath the resolved leg — `ONE TEAM BLANKED` / `CLEAN-SHEET PATH LIVE`. THE WORD `LIVE` ON A FINISHED MATCH, ONE SLOT FROM THE WORD `FT`.** `T108`'s law in the same frame as the ending it contradicts. **This is not a new rule and no new machinery is proposed: either the fixture boundary takes `§6.7`'s treatment, or there is no boundary because the legs share one telling — and `T140` is Allen's answer** | batch 128 · §2.1, §2.2

title: Two-plus legs dead at one whistle — `S85` says MORE than `T143` quoted, and the offer is NOT presented
body: Two-plus legs dead at one whistle — `S85` says MORE than `T143` quoted, and the offer is NOT presented | **RULED — and `T143`'s citation of `S85` is CORRECTED · DD 2026-08-21 batch 169, on the lead's question.** **`T143` reads: *"`S85` exactly: a refusal knowable before the act is SHOWN BEFORE IT, and the player must not spend a Whistle to discover the ticket was already dead twice over."* **`S85` SAYS: *"where a refusal is knowable BEFORE the act, the surface shows it before AND THE ACT NEVER HAPPENS."*** `T143` kept the first half and dropped the second — the same shape as `T103-am`, in the citation of a law rather than of a row.** **AND THE DROPPED HALF IS THE OPERATIVE ONE. `S85`'s substantive ruling is not disclosure, it is CATEGORY: *a price cell is BOTH a fact and an offer… AT THE LEG CAP AN UNAVAILABLE PRICE STOPS BEING AN OFFER AND REMAINS A FACT. The offer affordance goes; the price stays legible.* And its diagnosis names this exact failure: *A DEAD CLICK IS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A KNOWABLE REFUSAL IS LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED.*** **THE OBJECTION ANSWERED, because it is the lead's strongest: a Whistle at two-plus dead is not REFUSED — it performs, and saves a leg. **But the ticket is lost either way, so the saved leg buys nothing: the act does nothing IN THE ONLY CURRENCY THE TICKET HAS.** `S85`'s defect is *it told him he may act, and then did not act* — and here it costs him a SCARCE CONSUMABLE rather than a click, which makes the case stronger than the one `S85` was ruled on, not weaker.** **RULED: AT TWO OR MORE LEGS DEAD AT ONE WHISTLE, THE SAVE OFFER IS NOT PRESENTED FOR THAT TICKET. The consumable stays legible in inventory and is untouched — `S85`'s own shape (*the offer affordance goes; the price stays legible*) and `S69`'s transparent disabled `LOCK` before it. The item is not spent, not hidden, and not refused at the moment of the click; it is simply not offered against a ticket no single call can save.** **THE LEAD'S BUILD IS NOT WASTED AND SHOULD PROCEED: exposing `NoSingleCallSaves` FROM THE ENGINE IS REQUIRED UNDER EITHER ANSWER — it is what lets the surface either present-with-a-warning or not present at all. **Only the presentation changes, and presentation is phase 3.** Build the flag; wire the affordance to it.** **AND `T143`'s SENTENCE STANDS APART FROM ITS CITATION: *the player must not spend a Whistle to discover the ticket was already dead twice over* is exactly right, and this row is how it is delivered rather than a departure from it** | batch 169

title: One ladder, one unit; a ranking is not a per-element check
body: One ladder, one unit; a ranking is not a per-element check | **Law** · DD 2026-08-07 batch 13: (a) the ladder's unit is **Rec.709 luma on display-encoded values**, studio-wide, quoted with every number — three conventions produced a 0.21 gap where the truth is 0.047, and the mis-ranking lands exactly on the colour money lives in; (b) a per-element value check cannot see a ranking — emphasis is not one scalar (wax outranks toner by chroma; toner-2 outranks toner-3 by value); rankings are asserted against the composition in the channel that carries them. The fourth reporting axis: **unit** (with scope, coverage, resolution) | batch 13 **C33-am · batch 15**: where an L4 candidate is a filled field and its competitor is type, dominance is judged on ZONE MEAN and PEAK together, both reported — peak-vs-peak silently compares a field against a glyph and the field always loses while dominating the frame. TV gate V1 takes both columns. Second correction of the ladder's unit to see money properly **C33-am2 · batch 16**: an L4 ranking gate cannot see INTERNAL contrast — dominance and legibility are different instruments. V1 gains a companion: every element that inverts reports the contrast between its field and its own ink. Sixth vacuous-green shape this fortnight, first inside a single element (found as T68) **C33-am3 · batch 17 — three instruments, three spaces (LAW):** ladder = Rec.709 luma on display-encoded; contrast ratio = relative luminance in LINEAR; emission hue/chroma = CIELAB on linear authored. Every measurement states its SPACE as well as its unit; luma-parity values are measured, never linearly scaled; the three ladders are never compared (the EMIT gate had it right before either seat). Both seats' same-batch errors recorded (DD's display-encoded CR 3.18:1 vs the true 8.12:1; room's linear-scaled prediction over by 14.2%). Sixth reporting axis: **space**

C11's precondition. The FIFTH reporting axis: **reproducibility** (scope, coverage, resolution, unit, reproducibility) | batch 14

title: An element and its ground must not move together
body: An element and its ground must not move together | **Law** · DD 2026-08-08 batch 19 *(issued as "C34"; renumbered C35 in transcription — C34 [reproducibility] already existed from batch 14; collision reported to the DD)*: where an element and the surface behind it are driven by one control (ApplyBoost's Payout case drives text AND flood — ratio preserved at any amplitude), no brightness change can make the element readable. Legibility = stable ground + inverted ink, never a boosted pair. Third correction to the instrument family (C33-am2 dominance≠legibility; C33-am3 linear space; C35 boost-is-not-a-legibility-lever). Gate V8 extends: an inverting element reports whether its own ground is STATIC across the beat — a moving ground makes the ratio an instant, not a state | batch 19 **C35-am · batch 27: the contrast pair is what the EYE receives, not what the layers author — a compositor stack reads as one field**

title: A control must bracket the interval it certifies
body: A control must bracket the interval it certifies | **Law** · DD 2026-08-09 batch 20 (adopted batch 19, promoted on its founding case): a control certifies only the interval its samples enclose, checked by the other half of the instrument — never asserted by the half being checked. Opening pair brackets the warm-up; a closing control certifies the run. Founding case: an emission set passed control-a==control-b while the capture step mutated the room under it; two sets discarded. §4.2's temporal form. **Constitution §4.4 PROPOSED — awaiting Allen** | batch 20 **APPROVED — Allen 2026-08-09; constitution §4.4 canon**

title: A prediction from a contaminated frame is a floor, not a target
body: A prediction from a contaminated frame is a floor, not a target | **Law** · DD 2026-08-10 batch 29, **APPROVED — Allen, same day; constitution §4.6**: where an expected value derives from a frame that still contains the element under test, it is a FLOOR stated as a direction of travel — never a number to land on. Founding case: batch 27's 6.47/6.58 'pre-verified' band — _goldFlood at alpha 0 still fed 0.0269 of ground (an element at zero alpha is not an absent element; §2.5's shape one step earlier). Landing INSIDE the band would have meant residue survived — the pre-commitment had inverted its own test. Pre-commitment NOT weakened: expressing it as a VALUE is what failed; 'ground falls, ink stops moving' would have been satisfied exactly | batch 29

title: A freeze is checked against the seat's own OUTPUT, not only the lane's input
body: A freeze is checked against the seat's own OUTPUT, not only the lane's input | **Law (register-level, C39/C42/C43's standing — not proposed for the constitution)** · DD 2026-08-12 batch 38: where a freeze protects a verification pair, a routed **measurement** respects it by construction — measurements move no pixels and a lane reporting one is correctly freeze-clean. **The RULING that measurement produces may not be.** The freeze check therefore runs **at the moment of ruling, on what the ruling causes to change**, and **it is this seat's to run because the lane cannot see it**: from inside the lane the submission is freeze-clean and stays that way right up until someone rules on it. **Two founding cases, one batch apart, two different lanes:** **T80-am** — room's T65 settlement-cast measurement, where room stated the freeze was respected and that was true of a measurement and stopped being true when the measurement became a ruling that re-authored a value inside the pair's own frames; and **T82 / T80-am2** — TV's tabular measurement, identical shape, freeze-clean as a finding and a frozen variable the moment option (a) was granted. **Standing practice: any ruling issued while a verification pair is open states, IN THE RULING, whether it creates a frozen variable.** Two independent founding cases is what makes this a law at all; a third argues for promotion to constitution §4 beside the other instrument clauses | batch 38

title: A cross-element invariant is an ASSERTION or it does not exist
body: A cross-element invariant is an ASSERTION or it does not exist | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-13 batch 64, promoted from T95. **§3.5's enabling instrument.** **Where two elements are required to hold a relationship — the same rect, the same face, the same value, the same state — that requirement is expressed as a MACHINE-CHECKED ASSERTION, or it is not a requirement at all.** A relationship recorded in prose, in a comment beside the code, or in a reviewer's memory **is UNENFORCED**, and the first ruling that moves one element **breaks it silently and everywhere.** **Founding case:** `Score` is the punch overlay and **its own build comment stated the invariant verbatim** — *"Same text, SAME RECT, same face as `_tMatchup` … so superimposing it"* — yet both centre in their own box; T91-am re-bounded one of them and **the comment could not stop the other from staying where it was**, so the scoreline rendered doubled and illegible on every score change until frames caught it. **TV's own line is the clause's short form: A SHARED LOCAL IS A CONVENTION; AN ASSERTION IS A CONTRACT.** **Why this is a LAW and not a note — it is what makes §3.5 COMPLIABLE:** §3.5 obliges the dependent layout to be re-derived in the same commit as the bound that moved, but **nobody can re-derive a dependency they cannot SEE**, and this one was visible only to a reader of one comment in one file. **A rule requiring perfect recall is a rule that will be broken; C51 converts it into one an instrument keeps.** **Second catch of the same shape, named because it is why this promotes now:** C46-am2 found that **the code knew a worst case and the sweep did not use it** — *a worst case documented in a comment beside the generator is not a worst case the generator uses* — **the same defect class on a different instrument: knowledge recorded where nothing can act on it.** **Both instances are on the TV surface**, so this ships as a register-level law binding all four surfaces by its reasoning and **promotes to the constitution on a catch on a SECOND surface**; this seat does not promote to the constitution on one surface's evidence. **Scope, stated so it is not read wider than it is: this governs INVARIANTS BETWEEN ELEMENTS**, not every design decision — **a ruled value lives in the owning document; a required RELATIONSHIP between two elements lives in a test** | batch 64

title: A classification with no category for the truth will file the truth under a falsehood
body: A classification with no category for the truth will file the truth under a falsehood | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-17 batch 104, **promoted from the consolidated sweep's own §4.2**, which prints `UNACCOUNTED FOR — this number must be 0` and reports **12**. **The twelve stats-panel slots ARE covered** — by the panel's own pin — **but the instrument's only category for a slot it does not sweep is *declared unswept (renders no string)*, which is FALSE for all twelve. The invariant is LYING rather than GAPPING**, and it lies because the taxonomy left it nowhere true to put them. **THE GENERAL FORM: an instrument may report that it did not measure something; it may NOT assert a REASON it has not checked.** A category is a CLAIM, and a default heading applied for want of a better one is a claim made without evidence. **This is not a tooling nicety — it is batch 98 one level up**, where thirteen TV rows sat in the SureThing table because the structure put them where the heading said rather than where they belonged. **THE INSTRUMENT CHANGE, WORDED FOR BUILD — four clauses. (1) A THIRD CATEGORY: `DELEGATED`, meaning covered by a NAMED other instrument.** (2) **It must name that instrument, and the name must RESOLVE — a delegation to a name that does not exist is a lie with extra steps, so the sweep FAILS when the named instrument is absent.** Renaming or deleting a pin must break loudly, because the whole defect being fixed is a silent false claim. **(3) The must-be-zero line does NOT absorb it.** `UNACCOUNTED FOR = 0` stays a hard invariant on its own terms; delegated slots report on their OWN line with their count, their list and the instrument named — **a positive statement, never an absence.** A fix that quiets the alarm by widening what counts as accounted-for is the same defect with better manners. **(4) THE TRAP, AND IT IS THE CLAUSE MOST LIKELY TO BE MISSED: a delegation must distinguish COVERED from SCHEDULED.** *Covered* means the named instrument **has run and docked**. **`T101`'s residual was found in this very window to be "never run and never docked" rather than "no instrument"** — so a `DELEGATED` category that cannot express that would have reported the panel COVERED while it was in fact UNMEASURED, **recreating the identical lie one level higher and inside the fix for it.** **A delegation is a claim with its own staleness and must carry its own evidence date.** | `[TV] TvExtentSweep §4.2 · docs/handoffs/tv-theater.md`

title: A capture gate that asks whether a thing EXISTS will pass on a frame that does not SHOW it
body: A capture gate that asks whether a thing EXISTS will pass on a frame that does not SHOW it | **Law, cross-surface** · DD 2026-08-18 batch 113, **promoted from the markets-pregame lane's self-caught harness fault, which it found, fixed and recorded rather than shipping.** **The founding case: the first shoot PASSED and produced two frames that did not contain their own subjects** — `S3`'s `no prices offered` sat behind fourteen scorer rows below the fold, and `S1`'s PLAYERS line was below the fold. Both assertions used `GetComponentsInChildren`, **which finds objects that have scrolled out of view.** **Three of that set's six states would have docked as evidence of nothing, under a green run.** **THE LAW: EXISTENCE IN THE HIERARCHY IS NOT THE CLAIM A CAPTURE MAKES.** A capture asserts *this frame shows this thing*; a hierarchy query asserts *this thing was constructed*. **They agree exactly until a list scrolls, and then the green run is the lie.** **THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE THAT WILL BE MISSED — MEASURE IN-FRAME IN LOCAL SPACE, NEVER WORLD SPACE.** The stricter gate then failed twice, correctly: `IsInFrame` first compared **world-space** corners, and **this is a world-space canvas on a physical laptop in a room** — the entire 704px viewport spans about 0.1 world units, so every row rounds together; **and the screen is TILTED, so a world-space horizontal comparison is taken across a rotated plane and means nothing.** It measures in the viewport's **local space — the space the layout is authored in, whose units are the pixels every other constant on this surface is written in.** **KIN TO `C53` AND `C54`, and the family is now three: `C53` a classification with no category for the truth; `C54` an instrument reporting only the extremum; `C55` an instrument asserting the WRONG PREDICATE. All three are instruments making claims wider than their evidence, and all three passed green while doing it.** **The practice: a capture gate names the SUBJECT and asserts it is in frame, and the lists are scrolled to their feet before the shutter.** | `[ST] SureThingVisualCaptureTests · surfaces-evidence-dock-2026-08-18.md`

title: The discriminator is AUTHORSHIP, not emissibility — the pool follows the DECK, never the BUILD
body: The discriminator is AUTHORSHIP, not emissibility — the pool follows the DECK, never the BUILD | **CORRECTED — DD 2026-08-19 batch 125, §1.5. `C57` stands; its test does not.** **I ruled that *a pool missing a string the code CANNOT YET emit is CORRECT*, and treated "the build can emit it" as the discriminator. `TvExtentSweep`'s `DecisiveBeatLines` pool refutes it, deliberately and in writing:** it carries `ApproachUnder` and `TurnUnder` — **two cells `TheaterChoreographer.ResolveBeat`'s `gateEligible` can never fire, because it requires `countHelps` (Over) and §6 keeps the Under mirror out of scope** — and its own comment gives the reason: ***"a pool that includes a not-yet-reachable string is caught the moment anyone looks at it; a pool that OMITS one is invisible in the frames until the day it becomes reachable and nobody re-swept for it."*** **THAT IS RIGHT AND MY RULE WOULD HAVE CALLED IT A FABRICATED POOL.** **THE REAL DISCRIMINATOR, and the two cases are not the same thing wearing different clothes: (1) AUTHORED-AND-GATED — the string EXISTS IN THE SOURCE DECK and a scope gate keeps it from firing (`SweatFlavor.cs:297-319`). The pool SHOULD hold it: measuring it costs nothing and the day the gate opens the box is already certified. (2) RULED-AND-UNWRITTEN — the string exists in a REGISTER ROW and nowhere in the source (`RETURNED`, bare `CASHED OUT`, the suffix's removal). The pool MUST NOT hold it: that is `T111-am`'s fabrication, and a sweep that passes on a string the surface cannot construct measured nothing.** **SO: THE POOL FOLLOWS THE DECK — what is AUTHORED IN SOURCE — NEVER THE BUILD, which is only what a gate currently lets through.** **`C57`'s three-line test survives and sharpens: in the deck but not the build → the pool SHOULD hold it; ruled but not in the deck → the pool MUST NOT.** **And the lesson underneath is `C11`'s in a new place: I ruled a law about an instrument WITHOUT READING THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN REASONING.** `T111-am` found this sweep's pools fabricated two days ago and I generalised from that finding to a rule the same file already argues against, three hundred lines further down. **The instrument had thought about it more carefully than the law did** | batch 125

title: What a PIPED console transcript cannot carry — promoted on the second catch
body: What a PIPED console transcript cannot carry — promoted on the second catch | **Law (register-level, `C46`/`C55`'s standing — a PRACTICE clause about an instrument, not a product one) · DD 2026-08-24 batch 175, promoted from two independent catches in four days.** **THE CONSOLE IS SELF-SHOOTABLE AND THAT REMAINS TRUE — piping stdin into the exe is the studio's cheapest evidence and it has settled real questions. **What is now measured is its BLIND SPOTS, and they are not obvious from the outside.*** **(1) COLOUR — markets, `888cc6d`: *"`ConsoleColor` does not survive a redirect — zero escape bytes."* MEASURED, not inferred. `B9` was routed out of that lane for it and needs a human at a real terminal. **(2) INPUT-GATED STATE — this batch: `Hold` returns `Input.None` on `Console.IsInputRedirected`, so ANY state reached only through a keypress is unreachable in a piped run.** `K21`'s fast-forward is the instance; cash-out-by-key (`:487`) and the save prompt sit behind the same guard.** **THE CLAUSE: BEFORE PIPING A CONSOLE CAPTURE, ASK WHETHER THE SUBJECT NEEDS COLOUR OR A KEYPRESS. If either, the pipe cannot carry it and a transcript will come back CLEAN — which is worse than coming back empty, because a clean transcript against an unreachable state reads as evidence of absence.** **`C55` IN A SECOND MEDIUM: that law says a green capture proves nothing if the subject scrolled off. **This says the same about a subject that could not have been on the screen at all** — and both fail the same way, by returning something that looks like a pass.** **AND THE CONSTRUCTIVE HALF, because two blind spots do not make the instrument bad: what the pipe DOES carry is every string, every width and every line count — which is what the console's own §13 gates assert, and it is why `K21`'s route is a GATE rather than a re-shoot. **Where the pipe is blind, the exact-assertion style is not** | batch 175

title: Transiently empty PRINTS; permanently empty LEAVES — the taxonomy is what the game offers
body: Transiently empty PRINTS; permanently empty LEAVES — the taxonomy is what the game offers | **Law (register-level, `C46`/`C57`'s standing — not proposed for the constitution) · DD 2026-08-24 batch 179, on the question `T161-am2`'s removal spec exposed. Allen's lane assignment rides it.** **THE QUESTION: with DoubleChance offering nothing, does `DOUBLE CHANCE` still print as a labelled kind inside `RESULT` — a group that stays populated by Moneyline, Handicap and WinningMargin? `MarketDestinations.KindsOf` filters `TableOrder` by DESTINATION and never by offer count (`:140-143`), so today it would.** **§4.1 DOES NOT ANSWER IT, AND THE REASON IS THE RULING: *"Empty groups still print — `CORNERS … no prices offered`. **A racecard prints the race even when it is abandoned**, and it means the destination set is a constant — it never varies by matchup, so the page is authored once and never reflows."* **THAT WAS RULED ABOUT A GROUP EMPTY FOR ONE MATCHUP. It was never asked about a market removed from the game, because until (b) there had never been one.*** **THE ANALOGY BREAKS EXACTLY THERE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE RULING: an ABANDONED race is on the card and was not run TODAY. **A market removed from the offered set is a race THE MEETING NO LONGER HOLDS — and a racecard does not print those.** Printing `DOUBLE CHANCE … no prices offered` in every matchup forever does not report an absence; **it teaches a market that does not exist**, and it advertises to the player a thing he can never take, which is `S85`'s ground — *an offer that cannot be taken is not an offer.*** **AND §4.1's LOAD-BEARING REASON SURVIVES REMOVAL INTACT, which is what makes this safe rather than a trade: the constancy clause says the set *"never varies BY MATCHUP, so the page is authored once and never reflows."* **A SMALLER CONSTANT IS STILL A CONSTANT.** `TableOrder` is a `static readonly` array (`:125`); dropping a member leaves it just as invariant across matchups, the page still authored once, still never reflowing. **§4.1's layout argument does not require keeping the kind — it requires the set not to vary in play, and it does not.*** **RULED, AS A DISCRIMINATOR SO THE NEXT REMOVAL NEEDS NO RULING: **EMPTY FOR A MATCHUP → PRINTS**, with §4.1's `no prices offered`; the taxonomy is the constant and the emptiness is DATA. **EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION → LEAVES THE TAXONOMY**; the taxonomy is what the game OFFERS, and a kind that offers nothing in any matchup is not part of what the game offers. **The test is not *is it empty* but *can it ever be non-empty*.*** **SO `DOUBLE CHANCE` COMES OUT OF `TableOrder`, OUT OF `KindsOf(Result)`, OUT OF `For()` AND OUT OF THE LABEL MAP (`:161`) — the contents block and the destination page follow from those and need no separate edit.** **§4.1 IS NOT AMENDED. Its sentence is correct for its case and this row does not touch it; what is added is the boundary it never had, and `T161-am2`'s removal is the first thing to reach it.** **THE SCOPE CONSEQUENCE ALLEN ASKED FOR, and it is the reason this ruling sizes the lane: **the removal now touches `MarketDestinations.cs` as well as `MatchModel.cs`, and BOTH SURFACES re-derive from it** — the laptop's ENTRY sheet and the console's contents page. **Three fewer offers per matchup means the console's matchup-global line numbers RENUMBER below `RESULT`, and §5.1 rules those numbers ARE the pick addresses** (*"the printed line number is also the ADDRESS — and this is the whole design"*). Nothing persists an address, so nothing breaks — **but every pin on a count, a range or a folio moves with them, and §13's gates should be RE-RUN rather than assumed** | batch 179

title: The console's PAGE has never been authored — and 62 fails the pool by ONE character
body: The console's PAGE has never been authored — and 62 fails the pool by ONE character | **RULED — 80 columns × 24 rows** · DD 2026-08-19 batch 121, on `dd-import/console-read-2026-08-19/GEOMETRY.txt`. **`Ui.Rule()` prints 62 columns and that number is the title box's 60 plus two — taken from a decoration, never from content.** `C46` exactly: a fixed box carrying an unstated claim about what fits in it, and here the box is the whole screen. **MEASURED AGAINST THE ENUMERATED POOL per `S84`/`S96-am` — 320 constructible clubs, 144 players, never the seed's champion: the widest constructible row name is `SAN FRANCISCO SPREADSHEETS UNDER 4.5 CORNERS` at 44 characters, which is THE SAME CHAMPION `S96-am2` FOUND ON THE LAPTOP, arriving independently in a different medium.** Against 19 columns of fixed row chrome (line number, price, probability): **page 62 → a 43-column name field → FAILS BY ONE CHARACTER; page 80 → 61 columns → fits with 15 leader dots at the worst case.** **80 IS DERIVED TWICE OVER: the pool refuses 62, and the surface is ALREADY PRINTING AT 79 — its slate row. One of the two authored widths is wrong and it is the one that came from a title box** (`S94-cl`'s lesson on a second surface: the packing is derived from measured labels, not authored constants). **24 is the medium's floor** — the ANSI/VT100 standard and the Windows console default's usable height. **THE PAGE DOES NOT REFLOW: `Console.WindowHeight` throws on a redirected stream so a floor must exist regardless; a layout that reflows cannot be captured or gated (`C11`, `C18`); and a larger window HOLDS the page rather than changing it, which is what a printed page does.** **STATED CONSTANT per constitution §3.5 — written down once, every layout derives, nothing re-authors 62/79/80 locally.** **BLIND SPOT, per §4.2: a piped transcript has NO VIEWPORT — these captures show what the surface printed, never what the player saw. That blind spot is why this is a ruling at all: a surface that calls `Ui.Clear()` and then writes 92 lines has made the viewport the deciding element of its design, and no instrument in this studio is on it** | batch 121 · `spec-console-surfaces-2026-08-19.md` §3

title: The console's AUTHORITY — it inherits, and no owning document is commissioned
body: The console's AUTHORITY — it inherits, and no owning document is commissioned | **RULED** · DD 2026-08-19 batch 121. Constitution §1.1 lists four owning documents and **the console has none**; the phone precedent (`C26-am3`) says a surface in scope needs an authority to be judged against. **RULED: NO OWNING DOCUMENT. THE CONSOLE INHERITS.** Its **words, taxonomy, order and row grammar are the laptop's** (`spec-market-surfaces-2026-08-17.md` plus `S89`–`S102`) — it is not a fifth in-fiction surface, Reading B is off the table, and it needs no identity of its own. Its **evidence and authority rules are the constitution's**, unchanged. **`spec-console-surfaces-2026-08-19.md` is the authority for what the MEDIUM forces it to differ on — the page, the address, the pagination, the refusal points — and that list is short by construction.** **IF IT EVER GROWS PAST THAT LIST IT HAS STOPPED INHERITING AND THE QUESTION RETURNS TO ALLEN.** Commissioning a document for four differences would be the `08-art-direction.md` mistake in miniature — one document governing registers it does not own | batch 121 · §11

title: The per-side `GF`/`COR`/`CRD` block has no home on a 24-line page — ACCEPTED as a product loss, and the reason is SURFACE-SPECIFIC rather than a concession to the page
body: The per-side `GF`/`COR`/`CRD` block has no home on a 24-line page — ACCEPTED as a product loss, and the reason is SURFACE-SPECIFIC rather than a concession to the page | **RULED — ACCEPTED LOSS, with one condition that reopens it · DD 2026-08-21 batch 166.** **THE LOSS IS REAL AND IS NAMED RATHER THAN WAVED: the old detail screen's per-side goals-for, corners and cards gave TEXTURE that neither the record nor a price carries — a player comparing two corners markets across matchups loses a comparison he used to have. Zero slack on 24 lines means it has nowhere to go, and §11 puts THE PAGE on the short list of things this spec may differ from the laptop on.** **BUT THE PAGE IS NOT THE ARGUMENT, AND IF IT WERE, §11's OWN CLAUSE WOULD FIRE — *"if it ever grows past that list, it has stopped inheriting and the question returns to Allen."* Dropping CONTENT because the page is full is exactly the growth that clause is watching for.** **THE ARGUMENT IS §6.3, AND IT HOLDS ONLY ON THIS SURFACE: *"the console is the ONLY surface in the studio that prints all four"* of the four-number model — true probability, offered odds, stake, payout (`design/00-vision.md` §3). **THE `GF`/`COR`/`CRD` BLOCK IS THE MACHINE'S INPUTS. THE CONSOLE ALREADY PRINTS THE MACHINE'S OUTPUT, ON THE ROW, NEXT TO THE PRICE.** Form data is what a player uses to ESTIMATE a probability; this surface hands him the probability. On the laptop, on the TV and on the phone that block would be load-bearing — on the console it is the one place in the studio where it is not.** **AND THE CONTRAST IS DELIBERATE STUDIO LAW RATHER THAN AN ACCIDENT OF THIS SPEC: the TV BANS the win-probability numeral (`T16`, generalised at `T86-am` — *the match theatre prints FACTS and OFFERS, not OPINIONS*), and the console PRINTS it (§6.3, the vision clause, *"recorded so nobody removes it as a leak"*). Two surfaces, opposite rulings, both correct — and this loss is acceptable on exactly the surface where the probability is legitimately shown.** **WHAT SURVIVES, confirmed by markets: the RECORDS are on the slate (`San Francisco Spreadsheets (8-0)`, §10.2), so team identity and form-at-a-glance are not gone.** **THE CONDITION, PRE-COMMITTED: **IF THE TRUE-PROBABILITY COLUMN EVER LEAVES THE CONSOLE, THIS RULING REOPENS** — the whole argument rests on it, and a later seat removing `p 47%` as a leak (which §6.3 already anticipates) would silently take this ruling's ground with it. Recorded here so the two are found together** | batch 166
